drivingQuestion: Is Rabbi Yehuda's measure or the Rabbis' measure greater?

segments.he: פְּשִׁיטָא דְּשִׁיעוּרָא דְרַבָּנַן נְפִישׁ! דְּאִי סָלְקָא דַּעְתָּךְ שִׁיעוּרָא דְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה נְפִישׁ, רַבָּנַן – בְּשִׁיעוּרָא דְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה הֵיכִי עָבְדִי? וְאֶלָּא מַאי, שִׁיעוּרָא דְרַבָּנַן נְפִישׁ? רַבִּי יְהוּדָה – בְּשִׁיעוּרָא דְּרַבָּנַן מַאי עָבֵיד? אֶפְשָׁר דִּגְחִין וְחָלֵיף תּוּתֵיהּ.
segments.en: The Gemara answers: It is «obvious that the Rabbis’ measure» is «greater, as, if it enters your mind» that «Rabbi Yehuda’s measure» is «greater, how would the Rabbis act in» the circumstance of «Rabbi Yehuda’s measure?» It is clear that a camel will have to pass beneath the tree with a burden, and it would not be able to do so. The Gemara expresses surprise at this claim: «Rather, what» then would you say? That «the Rabbis’ measure» is «greater?» If so, «how would Rabbi Yehuda act in» the circumstance of «the Rabbis’ measure?» It is also clear that a camel will have to pass there with its rider. The Gemara answers: «It is possible for» the rider «to bend over and to pass underneath» the branches.
